compiled_state.description:
## Evidence — a REAL Jira DC instance, GitHub Actions run 30604756524

A writing reconcile pass (`--mode bootstrap-strict`) against the live J5 harness exits 1:

    ERROR: reconcile_once raised: 'JiraDataCenterTransport' object has no attribute
    'set_entity_property'

Found by story J7's new live module (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/test_reconcile_pass.py`) on its
FIRST real run. `--mode dry-run` passes; only the writing path crashes.

## Root cause — the PORT under-specifies what the CORE requires

`set_entity_property` is called from THREE core sites:

* `dispatch_one.py:321`     — `_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, jira_key, 'local_id', local_id)`
* `binding_store.py:517`    — `client.set_entity_property(keyed, 'local_id', local_id)`
* `apply_inbound_records.py:279` — `_call_with_retry(client.set_entity_property, ...)`

It is implemented in exactly ONE place: `adapters/jira/acli_rest.py:266` (Cloud).

And crucially it is **NOT a member of the `TicketTransport` Protocol** in `_backend.py`, which declares
only create_issue / get_issue / update_issue / transition_issue_by_name / add_label / search_issues.

So the core depends on a transport method the PORT never declares. That is why every structural check
passed while the real thing was broken: `isinstance(x, TicketTransport)` is satisfied without it, the
contract suite never calls it, and 1636 unit tests are green. The Protocol is not a faithful statement
of the core's requirements, so conformance to it proves less than it appears to.

This is the SAME CLASS of defect as J6's `add_label` bug (a method called with a shape `jira.JIRA`
never had). Both shipped because the only oracle was a fake that mirrored the author's assumption.

## Why it matters

Epic e369 exists to deliver Jira Server/Data Center support. With this defect a DC deployment cannot
complete a writing reconcile pass at all — the headline capability does not work. `local_id` entity
properties are the binding marker the reconciler plants to correlate remote issues with local tickets,
so this is not cosmetic: without it, binding/correlation cannot be established on DC.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `JiraDataCenterTransport` implements `set_entity_property` against DC's REST v2 entity-property
      endpoint, asserted by a live test that FAILS before the fix
- [ ] a full writing reconcile pass (`bootstrap-strict`) against the J5 harness exits 0/75 with no
      unhandled exception — i.e. J7's `test_a_repeated_dc_reconcile_pass_writes_nothing` and
      `test_a_dc_created_ticket_carries_the_shared_jira_provenance` PASS
- [ ] **`set_entity_property` is added to the `TicketTransport` Protocol** so the port states what the
      core actually requires, and a backend missing it fails `isinstance` instead of failing at runtime
- [ ] an AUDIT of the remaining core call sites for other transport methods absent from the Protocol
      (same technique: grep `client.<method>` in core modules, diff against the Protocol's members),
      with anything found either added to the Protocol or explicitly justified — otherwise this exact
      bug recurs on the next backend
compiled_state.title: DC writing reconcile pass crashes: transport lacks set_entity_property, which the port never declared
